title: VEED Pricing 2026: Plans, Limits and Free Tier
summary: VEED pricing spans free and paid plans with monthly or annual billing. Determine total costs, feature limits, and unexpected charges before choosing.
body_markdown:
## Automating What Happens After a VEED Export With Activepieces


Nothing about what VEED charges you changes with Activepieces, an open-source tool with an MIT-licensed core and **747 integrations** that chains apps together without code. It handles the chore that follows an export, so a team shipping many videos stops posting links by hand.


Check VEED's own integrations list first, because if the connection you need is already there, you don't need a second tool.


In the plan below, exports land in a shared Google Drive folder, which is where the flow starts. The steps run in this order:


1. Trigger: Google Drive, "New File", pointed at the export folder.
2. Action: Google Sheets, "Insert Row", with filename, link and date.
3. Action: Slack, "Send Message to Channel".
4. Test run.
5. Publish.


In five moves, the numbered list shows the whole flow. The order is the point: the test comes before publishing, so nothing posts to a live channel until you've seen it work once. The paragraphs below cover the fields.


Choose the Google Drive integration, select "New File", and name the specific folder your VEED exports go to. Leave the folder blank and the trigger watches more than you intended, so every unrelated upload fires the flow.


Keep the export folder separate from anything else people drop files into, and the automation stays quiet when it should.


### Actions: log, notify, hand off


First comes Google Sheets "Insert Row". Map three columns: filename, the file's share link, and the date. That sheet becomes the record of what was exported and when, which is useful the day someone asks which version went out.


Second comes Slack "Send Message to Channel". Pick the channel, then write a message that carries the filename and link from the trigger. The team sees the export without anyone typing a message.


"Hand off" means the sheet row and the Slack message are where a human takes over: an editor reviews, a manager approves. The flow doesn't judge the video; it only makes sure someone knows it exists.


Run the test with a real file in the folder, then check that the row appears and the message posts.


A run is 1 credit however many steps it has, so these three steps cost no more than one would against the 1,000 credits a month on the $0 Free plan. Publish only after both do.


If you export a handful of videos and tell your team in the usual way, the setup costs more attention than it saves. The same applies if VEED's native integrations already post where you need.


Build this when the manual step is being skipped or forgotten, not before.
